rows.title_full: AN ACT SYNCHRONIZING THE ELECTIONS OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS WITH THE KABATAANG BARANGAY MEMBERS IN A SIMPLIFIED MANNER, BEING NON-PARTISAN
rows.abstract: Rationale: The present separate elections for the barangay officials and the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) members entail too much time, resources and effort which could have otherwise been devoted to more fruitful economic and community development activities. More so, that our elections were being held on weekdays which had to be declared as public holidays if contrasted to the United States of America ( a fully developed country) and other democratic countries where election day is not declareda public holiday.  This keeps their economy going faster than ours, while our workforce suffers loss of productivity, and our studentry, loss of learning/traini ng hours. > Proposes SIMULTENEOUS ELECTIONS for barangay officials and Sangguniang Kabataaan (SK) members IN EVERY ZONE, ON APRIL 9, 2000, and ON THE SAME DATE EVERY FOUR (4) YEARS thereafter, udner a SIMPLIFIED PROCEDURE.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ORDAINING AND INSTITUTING A REVISED INSURANCE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill has for its purpose the revision and updating of certain provisions of the existing Insurance Code of the Philippines. It aims to further strengthen one of the most vital industries in our economy that contributes directly to the financial security of our people and which at the same time supports the economic development programs of the government. > With the globalization trend and modern technology upon us, several provisions in the present Insurance Code which was passed in 1978 have already become outmoded and in dire need of revision. > Proposes significant REVISIONS to the Code on the following areas: (1) suretyship; (2) margin of solvency; (3) Investment; (4) Insurance Commission; (5) Adjudicating power; (6) Juurisdiction; (7) Feesl and (8) Pre-need contract.

rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING THE MANUFACTURE OF PLASTIC BAGS. PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The indiscriminate and wanton disposal of plastic bags and other plastic materials has resulted in clogged sewers, rivers and drainage systems in Metro Manila and in other urban centers in the country. Plastics are non-biodegradal e and are thus not capable of being decomposed into benign and harmless elements under the action of normal environmental faces.  For a long, long time, these discarded plastics will pose great hazards to public health and welfare. Declares the following --- "SEC. 3. Penalty . - Any person found guilty of violating any provision of this Act shall be imposed the penalty of prision correccional in its maximum period and a fine of not less than ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (P100,000.00): Provided, however,that if the offender is a juridical entity, the penalty and fine hereinabove provided shall be imposed upon the chief executive officer, President or general manager found primarily responsible for the violation."

They give technical assistance to the governor or mayor by providing information and research data required for the delivery of basic servicesand adequate facilities to the public. rows.abstract: Rationale: "Investors are coming to MIndanao through purchase of land.  If the real properties purchased are free patent or homestead, the investors are encouraged to introduce any development or improvement because of the five-year right of repurchase by the vendor or his heirs. If the buyer introduces improvement thereon, he risks losing his investments should the vendor or his heirs exercise their right of repurchase. This hinders progress. > Seeks, therefore, to REPEAL the following provisions under Commonwealth Act No. 141: "Sec. 119. Every conveyance of land acquired under the free patent or homestead provisions, when proper, shall be subject to repurchase by the applicant, his widow or legal heirs within a period of five (5) years ffrom the date of the conveyance."

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION 291 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991", AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES(RE: SHARE OF LGUS IN THE NATIONAL WEALTH)
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Local Government Code which was enacted in 1991 provides for the empowerment of local government units.  To achieve a successful decentralizatio n of powers, the same Code rationalized the taxing powers of these local government unitsand their share in the national wealth. However, it has been observed that the share of local government units in the national wealth is not equitable. Mandates that local government units shall have a [one (1%) THREE PERCENT (3%) share of the grosssales or receipts of the preceding calendar year, derived by any government agency or government-owne d or-controlled corporation engaged in the utilization and development of the national wealth.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE CONSTRUCTION AND INSTALLATION OF UNDERGROUND SECONDARY STORAGE OR DOUBLE-WALLED TANK AS A REQUIREMENT PRIOR TO THE ISSUANCE AND/OR RENEWAL OF BUSINESS OR OTHER REGULAR PERMITS TO ANY OPERATOR OF GASOLINE STATION OPERATING AS BUSINESS FOR DISTRIBUTION/SE LLING OF GASOLINE, DIESEL AND OTHER SIMILAR PRODUCTS WITHIN THE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: The danger lies on the basic premise that any defect in the condition of the Underground Storage Tank (UST) of gasoline dealers can emit dangerous benzene and other toxic waste which may contaminate underground aquifer or water streams. If such condition happens, the people are in danger of contacting cancer, leukemia, asthma, mental disroder and in the worst scenario, the loss of lives. "Regulation of Gasoline Storage Facilities Act of 1997"  Aims to --- (1) institute an orderly system of law and order to properly regulate the system of retail selling of gasoline and its derivatives; (2) establish and sustain a balanced supply of gasoline; (3) contain the harmful effects of any damage in the storage tank; and (4) promote the efffective operation of the industry.

rows.title_full: AN ACT LIFTING THE BAN ON THE SLAUGHTER OF CARABAOS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED ELEVEN ENTITLED "AN ACT TO PROHIBIT THE SLAUGHTERING OF MALE AND FEMALE CARABAOS, HORSES, MARES AND COWS"
rows.abstract: Rationale: The following reasons have been advanced for the lifting of the ban: (1) It is ineffective; (2) EO 626 is conducive to violations; it cannot be relied upon to increase carabao population; and (3) The situation is still the same with or without the ban. > If the government wants to enhance the role of carabaos in Philippine agriculture, it should instead expand and improve the products that could be derived from carabao.  The ban limits this product to draft services. Researches haveproven that the animal could be an important source of meat and milk.  If this potential is fully exploited, it would go a long way in promoting equitable rural development.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING INCENTIVES TO THE SHIPBULDING AND SHIPREPAIR INDUSTRY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: "Until the early part of the 1970s, the Philippines was considered the leader and pioneer in shipbuilding and ship repair in the Asean Region. > This was the state of affairs in the industry until our neighbors generously grnated incentives to their own local shipbuilders and shiprepairers. As a result, their shipbuilding and shiprepair industry grew by leaps and bounds that by the turn of the decade the industry has become a pillar in their repective economies. > As a result, our shipbuilding and shiprepair industry was gradually eased out of the competition. In about a decade, our country was transformed from a vessel exporter to an importer of second-hand vessels." "Philippine Shipbuilding and Ship Repair Development Act of 11997" Seeks to grant incentives to shipbuilding and ship repair yards duly registered with MARINA, such as: (1) Exemption from import duties and value-added taxes;  (2) Facilitation of the government rules regarding entry, stay and departure of vesse
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1997-10-30

rows.author: B034
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING EMOTIONAL QUOTIENT ENHANCEMENT ACTIVITIES IN THE ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS CURRICULA AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Studies have confirmed that one's ability to cope with stress and to relate to his or her environment is more important than one's ability to process and absorb knowledge. Psychologists refer to the former as emotional quotient.  The latter is what we commonly known as intelligence quotient. "Emotional Quotient Enhancement Act" Provides, therefore, for the following --- "SEC. 2. The Department of Education, Culture and Sports (DECS) shall incorporate in the curricula of all public and private elementary and secondary schools nationwide, activities aimed at the enhancement of the emotional quotient of the pupils and students. SEC. 3. The Department of Science and Technology (DOST), in coordination with DECS, shall establish a staandard formula and set of activities for the purpose; Provided, that a school which may deem such standard to be insufficient may improve on the same, subject to the approval of the DECS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 1997-10-30

rows.author: B034
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REQUIRE STUDENTS IN ELEMENTARY AND HIGH SCHOOLS TO PLANT TREES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Because of need and greed, we have effectively and efficiently decimated a good portion of our forest lands.  This has resulted in various environmental and food security problems. Certainly, now is not just the time for conservation andprotection.  A lot of efforts should also be dedicated to rehabilitation of our forest resources . It is in this light  that the role of the youth , especially the students, in nation-building is being invoked. "Students' Tree Planting Act" Mandatesthe following --- "SECTION 3. Every elementary and high school student is hereby required to plant at least four trees every school year either in their oen lots or in areas designated in accordance with the provisions of this Act."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 1997-10-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING NATIONAL CEMETERIES AND PROVIDING FOR THEIR ADMINISTRATION AND MAINTENANCE
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is  proposed that a number of national cemeteries be established such that there will be at least one (1) national cemetery in each region and major island. In this way, the government can offer each veteran, military personnel and distinguished citizens a final resting place which provides both distinction for the departed and convenience for the relatives they leave behind. These national cemeteries shall be established individually by presidential proclamation and shall be placed under the Philippine Veterans Affairs Office. Mandates the establishment of  at least one (1) national cemetery in each region and major island to serve as a memorial and final resting place for veterans, military personnel and citizens who have rrendered distinguished service to the nation.
